# Designing Experiments in Computer Science

## Internal vs. External Validity

- **Internal**: did $X$ really cause the observed change in $Y$?
- **External**: does the result generalize?

## Randomization

- Run order of conditions.
- Workload-to-system assignment.
- Stochastic-algorithm seeds (report them).

## Blocking

Block on factors you cannot control (machine, time of day, dataset).

## Factorial Designs

A full factorial of factors A (3 levels) and B (4 levels) has 12 cells. With $n$ replicates per cell, estimate main effects and interactions.

## A Concrete Protocol

> *Question*: Does `-O3` reduce execution time vs. `-O2` on SPEC CPU 2017?
>
> *Design*: Paired, randomized run order, 30 runs per (benchmark, level), discard first 3 as warm-up, performance governor pinned.
>
> *Analysis (pre-registered)*: Per-benchmark median; paired Wilcoxon; bootstrap 95% CI; Cliff's delta.

Writing this down *before* you measure prevents p-hacking.
